method: Qualitative editorial assessments, not probabilities. Reading describes the wording needed for a placement; site describes the proposed locality; feature describes identification of the particular installation. Unresolved means that no specific feature has been established. Source counts are not independent confirmations.

entries.dependency: Adjacency in the list does not establish a continuous route. These edition comparisons are not new archaeological observations or independent readings of the metal.
entries.title: Sekakah valley: cairn or dam?
entries.readingNote: The heap word is interpreted as a cairn or as a dam; the feature type must be established separately.
entries.siteNote: Wadi Qumran remains conditional on its identification with Sekakah’s valley.
entries.featureNote: No individual cairn or dam is established as the entry’s landmark.
entries.finding: Puech’s cairn interpretation and the dam proposal require different searches. A reconstructed intake dam cannot settle the word.

features.name: Cairn in the valley
features.support: Fits Puech’s interpretation of the landmark word.
features.limit: No particular period cairn is identified.
features.test: Establish date and context independently of the aqueduct hypothesis.

features.name: Proposed intake dam
features.support: Fits the competing dam interpretation reported through Eshel/Luria.
features.limit: The dam is reconstructed; the original plan remains inaccessible.
features.test: Review the word and plan independently before equating this entry with entry 21’s intake.

entries.next: Review the landmark word and original survey; keep the cairn and dam models separate.

entries.title: Qumran: where does the conduit begin?
entries.readingNote: Conduit, head and Sekakah survive; the relation to Sekakah and the noun stone depend on restorations.
entries.siteNote: The water system fits the proposal, conditional on Sekakah referring to Qumran or its wadi.
entries.featureNote: No surveyed intake, particular stone or deposit is identified by the checked evidence.
entries.finding: The intake basin remains the first functional comparison. The Ilan–Amit chapter and figure index are located, but the plan pages require registered access; no feature geometry is verified.
entries.dependency: The six Phase 5 records are summaries and edition commentaries. Milik 1960 and 1962 repeat one identification; Eshel cites earlier surveys. They cannot be counted as six independent matches.

features.name: Intake basin and proposed dam position
features.support: Closest functional candidate for the head of a conduit.
features.limit: Stacey 2009 reports no surviving dam; its position is inferred. The reading does not independently identify this basin.
features.test: Read the original plan, distinguish surveyed remains from the reconstructed dam, and establish control points before narrowing the map.

features.name: Upper channel and run-off junction
features.support: An alternative beginning may be defined by the junction of different water-collection systems.
features.limit: This is a research alternative, not a published Copper Scroll identification established here.
features.test: Check construction phases and flow direction. A junction without the required relation to Sekakah would weaken this option.

features.name: Rock-cut tunnel mouth
features.support: A conspicuous element of the conduit system worth distinguishing from the intake.
features.limit: A tunnel opening is not automatically the head of the conduit.
features.test: Use the surveyed sequence of basin, channel and tunnel to test whether the opening could be the stated beginning.

features.name: Cistern outlet shown in Ground view
features.limit: The photograph does not show the upstream intake or the restored great stone.
features.test: Retain as context; do not use its highlight to select an entry 21 feature.

entries.next: Obtain the complete Ilan–Amit chapter and uncropped Fig. 1, then test its intake, junctions and tunnels against each permitted reading. Independent reading remains pending.

entries.dependency: Adjacency in the list does not establish a continuous route. These edition comparisons are not new archaeological observations or independent readings of the metal.
entries.title: Sekakah: east of which reservoir?
entries.readingNote: The edition specifies a fissure east of the reservoir; its name does not identify a surviving pool.
entries.siteNote: Qumran remains a candidate under the Sekakah identification.
entries.featureNote: Neither the named reservoir nor its eastern fissure is identified.
entries.finding: The east relation is a useful test. A nearby fissure alone does not satisfy it.

features.name: Period reservoir and eastern fissure
features.support: Qumran contains water-storage installations to compare.
features.limit: No checked evidence independently establishes the Solomon name for a particular pool.
features.test: Select a dated reservoir independently, then test the eastern relation; retain alternatives if the name cannot be resolved.

entries.next: Correlate reservoir phases and fissures on a source plan. Do not use Jerusalem’s similarly named pool to relocate Sekakah.

entries.dependency: Adjacency in the list does not establish a continuous route. These edition comparisons are not new archaeological observations or independent readings of the metal.
entries.title: The channel: Solomon or Shallum?
entries.readingNote: Puech allows Shallum rather than Solomon. The large landmark may be a boulder or, in other interpretations, a mound or sepulchral feature.
entries.siteNote: Qumran remains a possible locality; the link to entry 22 is conditional.
entries.featureNote: The channel and distance endpoints are unidentified.
entries.finding: The alternative name weakens the proposed reservoir-to-channel link. The stated distance cannot locate a feature while both endpoints are unknown.

features.name: Channel linked to entry 22’s reservoir
features.support: Possible if the name refers to Solomon and both entries concern the same water system.
features.limit: Shared ownership and hydraulic connection are not established.
features.test: Check the letter division before testing a connected reservoir and channel.

features.name: A channel associated with Shallum
features.support: A reading explicitly considered by Puech on p. 189.
features.limit: It supplies no identified local installation.
features.test: Keep this branch separate; independently identify the channel and large landmark before using the stated distance.

entries.next: Independent review of V 8–9, followed by a plan comparison. No distance buffer is drawn.

entries.dependency: Adjacency in the list does not establish a continuous route. These edition comparisons are not new archaeological observations or independent readings of the metal.
entries.title: Kippa: the approach from Jericho
entries.readingNote: The route relates Jericho and Sekakah; Puech’s northern-bank placement is an interpretation.
entries.siteNote: Wadi Kuteif remains a proposed ravine, not a securely named match.
entries.featureNote: The reported rock-cut chamber is undated and does not establish the required tomb.
entries.finding: Use the Jericho approach as a regional test. The list does not specify a journey from entry 23 to this tomb.

features.name: Tomb on a Jericho–Sekakah approach
features.support: Matches the kind of relationship described by the entry.
features.limit: No dated tomb and ancient approach have been correlated here.
features.test: Compare ancient access routes and securely dated tombs before choosing a bank or chamber.

entries.next: Check the original tomb record and route evidence, with alternative Sekakah placements retained.

entries.title: Doq: fortress or drying place?
entries.readingNote: Puech reads a drying place; Milik and other editions read a guardhouse or fortress.
entries.siteNote: The summit remains the preferred Doq proposal; the spring name alone cannot select it.
entries.featureNote: Neither the specified eastern corner nor a period drying installation has been established.
entries.finding: Fortress archaeology cannot decide the disputed landmark word.
entries.dependency: The ten records include regional cave occupation. Occupation of the mountain does not independently attest the required building corner.

features.name: Summit fortress corner
features.support: Compatible with the guardhouse or fortress reading.
features.limit: Later construction complicates the surviving plan.
features.test: Identify a securely dated eastern corner before claiming a feature match.

features.name: Drying installation at Doq
features.limit: No corresponding installation is established in the checked records.
features.test: Seek documented surfaces and their function; an empty search is inconclusive where preservation is poor.

entries.next: Request a blind comparison of the disputed letters in VII 11 before preferring a building type.

entries.title: Choziba: which outlet and which wall?
entries.readingNote: Koziba competes with Lefkovits’s Buz reading. The second landmark may mean retaining wall, parapet, mountain or rock.
entries.siteNote: Wadi Qelt remains the preferred locality under the Koziba interpretation.
entries.featureNote: The monastery anchor does not locate the ancient water outlet or date a particular wall.
entries.finding: Separate the spring head, the Jisr ed-Deir distribution point and the cliffside wall. They perform different functions.
entries.dependency: Six Phase 5 records include editorial identifications and survey summaries. The nineteenth-century survey is an observation source; its masonry dating is provisional.

features.name: ʿAin Qelt spring and channel head
features.support: Fits an outlet understood as a spring or the start of an aqueduct.
features.limit: The name and second landmark still need independent support.
features.test: Identify which period channel left the spring, and whether the required second landmark belongs to that same phase.

features.name: Jisr ed-Deir channel division
features.support: The Survey of Western Palestine records a distribution point here.
features.limit: A division is not necessarily the outlet intended by the text.
features.test: Compare the junction’s function and dated construction against the spring-head interpretation.

features.name: Wall opposite Deir el-Kelt
features.support: The survey records upper and lower channels against the cliff.
features.limit: Visible fabric alone does not establish a Second Temple retaining wall.
features.test: Check the wall’s construction sequence and its relationship to an independently located outlet.

entries.next: Match original plans to the three feature classes, then distinguish ancient construction from later repairs.

entries.title: Siloam: separate the name, pool and trough
entries.readingNote: Puech’s Siloam reading requires a disputed letter and restoration; competing editions read personal names or another installation.
entries.siteNote: Conditional on the Siloam reading. The earlier high rating remains withdrawn.
entries.featureNote: A period trough corresponding to the entry has not been established.
entries.finding: Szanton’s plans distinguish the tunnel-outlet pool from Birkat el-Ḥamra. Their names and the dating evidence must be evaluated separately.
entries.dependency: Several reports concern the same pool and street excavations. Repeated use of the label Siloam is not an independent reading of the scroll.

features.name: Silwan pool and tunnel outlet
features.support: Szanton proposes this as the Early Roman Siloam pool.
features.limit: The publication does not identify the scroll’s trough.
features.test: Compare the stratigraphy, plan and sections with the required installation after the wording is reviewed.

features.name: Birkat el-Ḥamra, the large stepped pool
features.support: Other excavation reports call this Siloam; Szanton proposes Solomon’s Pool.
features.limit: Its stepped form does not locate a particular trough.
features.test: Keep both naming hypotheses visible; identify which physical requirement could distinguish them.

entries.next: Have X 15–16 read independently of the pool names; then test the surviving trough/gutter requirement against original plans.

entries.title: Bethesda: a name or a reservoir complex?
entries.readingNote: Only Milik’s emendation supplies Bethesda. The reservoir wording does not uniquely name St Anne’s.
entries.siteNote: Bethesda remains a candidate; the twin-pool description also permits comparisons elsewhere.
entries.featureNote: No particular small, accessible basin has been identified as the scroll’s feature.
entries.finding: The Bethesda excavation reports cited by the editions still need direct checking.
entries.dependency: The recovered assessment explicitly says Vincent–Abel and Jeremias were cited through other authors. Their findings have not been independently audited here.

features.name: St Anne’s reservoir complex
features.support: A proposed match for a complex containing more than one reservoir.
features.limit: The place-name identification depends on an emendation.
features.test: Read the original excavation plans and determine which basin and access arrangement satisfy the wording.

features.name: Sisters of Sion double-pool comparison
features.support: A second double-pool setting recorded by Warren.
features.limit: This is a control comparison, not a newly endorsed placement.
features.test: Compare chronology, basin hierarchy and access under the same textual requirements.

entries.next: Review XI 12–13 and the original excavation publications before increasing site confidence.

qumranReview.access: Source-access record, edition comparison and separate spatial tests. No georeferencing or external specialist review has been completed.
